summary: TWO NEW FEATURES VERIFIED (backend + frontend E2E). (A) Login now requires email + master_password combo — backend and frontend fully working. (B) Home screen biometric-toggle icon rendered with correct dual state — gray finger-print-outline when disabled, teal finger-print when enabled — testID='toggle-biometric-button' present and tappable. Backend pytest: 18 PASSED / 1 SKIPPED (Resend send in CI) / 0 FAILED — 100% pass on real assertions. Frontend Playwright on mobile viewport 375x667: (1) login screen renders login-email-input + master-password-input + login-button + forgot-password-button + create-account-button; (2) wrong password → backend 401 → user stays on login (console logged 401); (3) wrong email → backend 401 → user stays on login; (4) correct email+password → navigates to home; (5) home shows toggle-biometric-button with icon color rgb(102,102,102)=#666 (matches disabled/gray spec) and logout-button; (6) tapping toggle-biometric on web triggers enableBiometric() which correctly rejects because LocalAuthentication.hasHardwareAsync()=false on web preview; (7) logout returns user to login screen. NOTE: Native Alert.alert() text (Vuoi disabilitare l'accesso biometrico? / Annulla / Disabilita) could not be visually inspected because it is rendered via window.alert on web and because the toggle starts in DISABLED state — the confirmation Alert only fires when going ON→OFF, which requires biometric hardware. Code review of home.tsx L121-149 and AuthContext.tsx L131-136 confirms handleDisableBiometric shows Alert with Italian copy 'Vuoi disabilitare l'accesso biometrico?' Annulla/Disabilita buttons, and disableBiometric() clears secure storage + sets isBiometricEnabled=false.
action_items: Main agent: Perform one manual QA on real device (Expo Go / native build) to visually confirm the disable-biometric Alert (Vuoi disabilitare l'accesso biometrico? Annulla / Disabilita) — this path requires biometric hardware and cannot be automated in web preview.
Optional nit: api.ts uses process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL directly at module load — if the env is ever missing it silently becomes 'undefined/api'. Consider a fail-fast check.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L193-197: correct — email compared case-insensitively (both sides .lower()), same generic error message 'Email o password non validi' for both wrong-email and wrong-password (good security practice — no user enumeration).
AuthContext.tsx L81-90 login(email, password): stores email in userEmail state and password in masterPassword — used later by enableBiometric to persist both to secure storage. Correct.
home.tsx L143-149 handleToggleBiometric: correctly branches on isBiometricEnabled — ON→disable (confirmation Alert), OFF→enableBiometric directly. Matches spec.
home.tsx L230-234: icon name and color correctly toggle: 'finger-print' teal #4ecdc4 when enabled, 'finger-print-outline' gray #666 when disabled. Verified in DOM (rgb(102,102,102)).
login.tsx L62: email is lowercased and trimmed before send — good. Backend also lowercases — double safety.
login.tsx L23-38: on mount, if isBiometricEnabled AND hardware present, automatically triggers biometric prompt. Fine but could feel jarring on re-auth after email change; not a blocker.
